CONTEXT. The previous page computes cos(180°/17), the 17-gon work of c. 1796. The next page tabulates 1 + Σ_{p≤x} 1/p over primes (1.8333 = 1+1/2+1/3, 2.0333, 2.17619, …) and compares it with ln ln x. It also contains Gauss's notes '1+1/2+…+1/n = ln n + C' and dx/(x lx). This page is a parallel computation of the sum of the reciprocal squares of the primes, P(2) = Σ_p p^{-2}.

NOTATION (my reading, confirmed by the numbers below). l(s) = log ζ(s), with ζ(s) = Σ n^{-s}. (s) = P(s) = Σ_p p^{-s}, the prime zeta function.

1. Euler product. log ζ(2) = Σ_p Σ_k p^{-2k}/k. Gauss writes this as l(2) = (2) + ½(4) + ⅓(6) + ¼(8) + …

2. Removing the even k. ½ l(4) = ½(4) + ¼(8) + …, so l2 − ½ l4 = (2) + ⅓(6) + ⅕(10) + 1/7(14) + …

3. Removing multiples of 3. ⅓ l6 − ⅙ l12 = ⅓(6) + 1/9(18) + … (the transcription shows only the first term). Hence l2 − ½l4 − ⅓l6 + ⅙l12 = (2) + ⅕(10) + 1/7(14) + 1/11(22) + …

4. Continuing the sieve. Gauss adds −⅕ l10 + 1/10 l20 + 1/15 l30. The coefficients are exactly μ(n)/n: n = 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15 give +1, −½, −⅓, −⅕, +⅙, +1/10, +1/15. In modern form this is Möbius inversion: P(2) = Σ_{n≥1} μ(n)/n · log ζ(2n). The n = 30 term is not written; it is negligible.

5. Closed form of the leading terms. Gauss uses Euler's ζ(2n) = 2^{2n−1}|B_{2n}|π^{2n}/(2n)!. This explains the side fragments '2aππ/1.2' and the factorial/691 quotients, which are Bernoulli-number bookkeeping with B12 = 691/2730.
- l2 − ½ l4 = log[(π²/6)/(π²/√90)] = ½ log(90/36) = ½ log(5/2).
- −⅓ l6 + ⅙ l12 = −⅙ log(ζ(6)²/ζ(12)). With ζ(6) = π⁶/945 and ζ(12) = 691π¹²/638512875, this ratio is 638512875/(691·893025) = 715/691. So the term equals −⅙ log(715/691).
- The side fractions 715 = 5·11·13, 6435 = 9·715 and 57915 = 81·715 are reductions of this ratio.

6. Numerics, lower left column, read with 13-place logs.
- ln5 = 1.6094379124341 and ln2 = 0.6931471805599, so ln(5/2) = 0.9162907318742.
- Half of this is 0.4581453659371.
- ln(715/691) = 0.0341427189263 (right column); one sixth is 0.0056904531544.
- 0.4581453659371 − 0.0056904531544 = 0.4524549127827.
- Next he subtracts ⅕ l10 = 0.000198820714 (entry later struck), giving 0.4522560920687.
- Then he subtracts 1/7 l14 ≈ 0.0000087492, giving 0.4522473428687.

7. Side computations of the small terms, bottom right and middle.
- 99457 → −49 → 99408: ζ(10) − 1 = 0.00099457…, minus half its square, gives log ζ(10) = 0.00099408. Dividing by 5 gives 19881, i.e. ⅕ l10 = 0.000198816. This corrected value replaces the struck 0.0001988207.
- 21677 = 1/11 l22 ≈ 2.1677e−8.
- 114 = 1/13 l26 ≈ 1.146e−9.
- 266 = 1/14 l28 ≈ 2.66e−10.
- 62 = 1/15 l30 ≈ 6.2e−11.
- 1/10 l20 ≈ 9.54e−8 is also needed; its entry is not identifiable with certainty.
- The partial sums 1.3611111 = 1 + 1/4 + 1/9 and 1.401111 = +1/25 are direct partial sums of 1 + Σ1/p², presumably as a control.
- With the corrected ⅕ l10 and these terms, the sum gives 0.4522474200…, the correct value of P(2) = 0.45224742004106…

8. Right margin (sideways). A series 'llx + lx/la + ½(lx/la)² + ⅓(lx/la)³ … + ½ + 1/(2·2)', the remarks 'x = √a', 'lla − l2' and 'Ve − 1', and the integrands (1/x²)lx and (1/x)lx. These appear to be heuristics for Σ1/p ≈ ∫dx/(x ln x) = ln ln x. For example, ln ln a − ln ln √a = ln 2 for primes between √a and a. The '1/(2·2)' suggests the series ln ln x + Σ (ln x)^n/(n·n!) for the logarithmic integral. This is my tentative reading and is fragmentary.

9. Circle diagram. p:x = √(vv − pp/4) and yy = x(p − x): the elementary chord/mean-proportional relation in a circle, unrelated to the rest.
errors: The written formula reads '½ l(5/2) + ⅙ l(715/691)', but the correct sign is minus. The term −⅓ l6 + ⅙ l12 equals −⅙ log(ζ(6)²/ζ(12)) = −⅙ log(715/691). Gauss's numerics do subtract (0.4581453659 − 0.0056904532), so this is only a slip in writing.

The first value used for ⅕ log ζ(10), 0.000198820714, is too large by about 4.5e−9; the true value is 0.000198816174. It is struck through and recomputed in the margin as 0.00019881(6) (99457 − 49 = 99408, /5). The running total 0.4522560920687 still carries the old value.

The intermediate total 0.4522473428687 is about 7.7e−8 below the true P(2). This is exactly the size of the not-yet-applied terms +1/10 l20 − 1/11 l22 − 1/13 l26 + 1/14 l28 + 1/15 l30 ≈ +7.29e−8, plus the 4.5e−9 error above. It is not an error, just an unfinished sum.
The line '⅓ l6 − ⅙ l12 = ⅓(6)' gives only the first term (the full series is ⅓(6) + 1/9(18) + …). This is harmless shorthand.

results.what: log ζ(s) = Σ_k P(ks)/k (logarithm of the Euler product) and its Möbius inversion P(2) = Σ μ(n)/n · log ζ(2n), derived by successive sieving
results.modern_name: Möbius inversion formula for the prime zeta function P(s) = Σ_n μ(n)/n log ζ(ns)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (computations of Σ1/p^n via log ζ, 1740s–1775); in general form Glaisher (1891), Landau–Walfisz (1920)

results.what: Closed forms log ζ(2) − ½ log ζ(4) = ½ log(5/2) and ζ(6)²/ζ(12) = 715/691 via Bernoulli numbers
results.modern_name: Euler's evaluation of ζ(2n) in terms of Bernoulli numbers

results.what: Numerical value Σ_p 1/p² ≈ 0.45224742 to about 9–10 decimals using 13-place logarithms
results.modern_name: Value of the prime zeta function P(2) = 0.4522474200410654…

results.what: Marginal heuristic linking Σ1/p to ∫dx/(x ln x) = ln ln x and series in ln x (cf. the next page's table of Σ1/p)
results.modern_name: Mertens' second theorem Σ_{p≤x}1/p = ln ln x + M + o(1) (heuristic form); logarithmic integral series
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (heuristic, 1737), Mertens (1874, proof); Gauss's prime-density heuristics known from 1849 letter to Encke

deep.surprise_reason: The method (log of the Euler product, Möbius-type sieving of log ζ(2n)) and the value of Σ1/p² are Euler's. The page shows Gauss independently reproducing them, apparently c. 1796 next to the 17-gon work and his Σ1/p tables. He makes neat use of the Bernoulli closed forms (the 715/691 ratio) and gets about 10-digit accuracy. It is a nice unpublished detail of his early analytic number theory, but contains nothing beyond Euler.
